answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because haven only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, pulse is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any signal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
